builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ConvLUT: Rethinking Convolutional Architectures for Ultra-Low-Latency LUT-Based Inference
summary: ConvLUT replaces conventional convolutional inference (GPU/CPU kernels) with fully unrolled lookup-table networks mapped directly onto FPGA logic, using LUT-tree convolution, channel-partitioned LUT pooling, and hardware-aware iterative pruning. The cost is a specialized FPGA design and synthesis pipeline, tight fan-in constraints that limit model capacity, and accuracy that remains only competitive rather than superior on small-scale benchmarks. Adoption can fail because the workflow requires FPGA hardware and HDL tooling, the method is validated only on tiny vision/audio tasks, and accuracy may degrade on realistic datasets outside CIFAR-10, Visual Wake Words, and Keyword Spotting.
rationale: The reader has a single GPU or third-party APIs and no FPGA toolchain, so this FPGA-specific LUT architecture is outside their production infrastructure.
technique: LUT-based convolutional networks for FPGA inference

claims.statement: ConvLUT replaces conventional convolutional inference (GPU/CPU kernels) with fully unrolled lookup-table networks mapped directly onto FPGA logic, using LUT-tree convolution, channel-partitioned LUT pooling, and hardware-aware iterative pruning. The cost is a specialized FPGA design and synthesis pipeline, tight fan-in constraints that limit model capacity, and accuracy that remains only competitive rather than superior on small-scale benchmarks. Adoption can fail because the workflow requires FPGA hardware and HDL tooling, the method is validated only on tiny vision/audio tasks, and accuracy may degrade on realistic datasets outside CIFAR-10, Visual Wake Words, and Keyword Spotting.

Fully unrolled inference latency below ~50 ns on MLPerf Tiny benchmarks, with at least an 8844x latency reduction over non-logic-based prior implementations on CIFAR-10 and at least 20 pp higher test accuracy than existing MLP-style LUT-based models on the same task.
